questions.title: Grid Word Exists
questions.prompt: Given a grid of characters and a word, return True if the word can be formed by moving up, down, left, or right without reusing a cell in the same path.
questions.hint: Try DFS from every cell that could be the first character, marking a cell while it is in the current path.

questions.title: Count Islands
questions.prompt: Given a grid containing 0 and 1, count connected groups of 1s. Cells connect only up, down, left, and right.
questions.hint: Every unvisited land cell starts one new island; flood-fill it so it is not counted again.

questions.title: Shortest Grid Route
questions.prompt: In a 0/1 grid, move up, down, left, or right through 0 cells only. Return the minimum number of moves from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell, or -1 if impossible.
questions.hint: Use BFS because every move has the same cost.

questions.title: Dependency Order
questions.prompt: There are n tasks numbered 0 through n-1. Each pair [task, prerequisite] means prerequisite must come first. Return one valid order, or [] if a cycle makes completion impossible.
questions.hint: Use indegrees and process nodes with indegree zero using Kahn's topological sort.
questions.solution:
def dependency_order(n, prerequisites):
    from collections import deque
    graph = [[] for _ in range(n)]
    indegree = [0] * n
    for task, pre in prerequisites:
        graph[pre].append(task)
        indegree[task] += 1
    q = deque(i for i in range(n) if indegree[i] == 0)
    order = []
    while q:
        node = q.popleft()
        order.append(node)
        for nxt in graph[node]:
            indegree[nxt] -= 1
            if indegree[nxt] == 0:
                q.append(nxt)
    return order if len(order) == n else []

questions.title: Grid Paths With Blocks
questions.prompt: A 0/1 grid uses 0 for open cells and 1 for blocked cells. Starting at the top-left, move only right or down. Return the number of distinct paths to the bottom-right.
questions.hint: Let dp[c] store the number of ways to reach the current row at column c.
